snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\) for some \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), and put \(m=2n\). For a sample \((T_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m\), define
\[
\overline T=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mT_i,\qquad
\overline Y=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_i,\qquad
\widehat C=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mT_iY_i-\overline T\,\overline Y,
\]
\[
\widehat V=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mT_i^2-\overline T^2,\qquad
\widehat\beta^{\rm deg}=\Pi_{[-3,3]}\!\left(\frac{\widehat C}{\widehat V\vee(1/6)}\right),
\]
where \(\Pi_{[-3,3]}(z)=\max\{-3,\min\{3,z\}\}\). Then, for every fixed \(F_\mu,F_\pi\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes m}}\left|\widehat\beta^{\rm deg}-\beta(P)\right|\le \frac{648}{\sqrt m}.
\]

defs.def:mean-zero-plm-family: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P_{\beta,v,\mu,\pi}^{0}:X\sim\nu_d,\ \mu\in F_\mu,\ \pi\in F_\pi,\ T=\pi(X)+u,\ \mathbb E[u\mid X]=0,\ \mathbb E[u^2\mid X]\equiv v\ge1/3,\ Y=\beta T+\mu(X)+\varepsilon,\ \mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0,\ |\beta|\vee|v|\le3,\ |T|\vee|Y|\le3\}\). This is the mean-zero full two-nuisance PLM consistent with equations (1.1) and (3.2) of \cite{gu2026optimally}.
defs.def:non-atomic-hard-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi):P(T=t)=0\text{ for every }t\in[-3,3]\}\).

assumptions.ass:two-n-iid: The \(2n\) observations are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the frozen core, the answer to the fixed-class product-converse question is negative. In particular, the allowed reference law \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\), for any \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), has the following property: for every \(n\), every fixed \(F_\mu,F_\pi\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) whose non-atomic subclass is nonempty, and the \(2n\)-sample experiment,
\[
\inf_{\widehat\beta_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)}
\int\left|\widehat\beta_n(o_{1:2n})-\beta(P)\right|\,dP^{\otimes2n}(o_{1:2n})
\le \frac{648}{\sqrt{2n}}.
\]
Consequently, for every sequence in \(\mathcal R_n^{\rm asym}\), the displayed risk is \(o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n})\) uniformly over all fixed class pairs, so no positive \(c\) and \(N\) with the property posed in the open question can exist for this allowed reference law.

defs.def:admissible-truth-classes: \(\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta)=\{F\subseteq\mathcal T_3:\exists G\subseteq\mathcal T_3,\ \sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(\nu_d)}\le\delta^{\rm appr},\ \sup_{\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)/(3\delta)\le\delta^{\rm stoc}\}\), where \(\bar\delta=(\delta^{\rm appr},\delta^{\rm stoc})\).

assumptions.ass:uniform-approximation: A pair \(F,G\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) obeys \(\sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(\nu_d)}\le\delta^{\rm appr}\).
assumptions.ass:localized-critical-radius: A learner class \(G\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) obeys \(\sup_{\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)/(3\delta)\le\delta^{\rm stoc}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every sequence in \(\mathcal R_n^{\rm asym}\), the displayed expressions satisfy \(\mathsf U_n\asymp s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\) and \(\mathsf L_n=o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n})\).

defs.def:a1-displayed-benchmarks: In Appendix A.1 of \cite{gu2026optimally}, the outcome error is denoted \(\varepsilon_Y\), and its condition is \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_Y\mid X,T]=0\). Theorem A.1 displays \(n^{-1/2}+[\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})^2]\wedge[(\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})(\delta_\pi^{\rm appr}+\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})]\) and \(n^{-1/2}+[\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})^2][\delta_\pi^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})^2]+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc}\wedge\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})^2\). At the proposed budgets these define \(\mathsf U_n=n^{-1/2}+\min\{s_{\mu,n}^2,s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\}\) and \(\mathsf L_n=n^{-1/2}+s_{\mu,n}^2s_{\pi,n}^2+s_{\pi,n}^2\). The paper uses \(2n\) observations, which changes only constants.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\) for some \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\). There is a numerical constant \(c_0>0\) such that, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every pair of budgets \(\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi\in[0,1]^2\),
\[
\frac{c_0}{\sqrt{2n}}\le m_{\rm PL}^{0}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)\le\frac{648}{\sqrt{2n}}.
\]
Moreover, for every sequence \((\bar\delta_{\mu,n},\bar\delta_{\pi,n})\in\mathcal R_n^{\rm asym}\) and every fixed \(F_{\mu,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\mu,n})\) and \(F_{\pi,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\pi,n})\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\beta_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_{\mu,n},F_{\pi,n})}\int\left|\widehat\beta_n(o_{1:2n})-\beta(P)\right|\,dP^{\otimes2n}(o_{1:2n})\le\frac{648}{\sqrt{2n}}=o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}).
\]
Consequently, the fixed-class product converse posed in the open-ended question is false under the frozen core: a product-scale converse requires an additional covariate-richness condition.

This is the mean-zero full two-nuisance PLM consistent with equations (1.1) and (3.2) of \cite{gu2026optimally}.
defs.def:non-atomic-hard-subclass: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi):P(T=t)=0\text{ for every }t\in[-3,3]\}\).
defs.def:mean-zero-fixed-class-risk: \(m_{\rm PL}^{0}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)=\sup_{F_\mu\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\mu)}\sup_{F_\pi\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\pi)}\inf_{\widehat\beta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)}\int|\widehat\beta(o_{1:2n})-\beta(P)|\,dP^{\otimes2n}(o_{1:2n})\). The infimum occurs after selection of the fixed class pair, so the estimator may know the truth classes, learner witnesses, and budgets.
